claims.claim: Model Studio's international regions are Beijing, Virginia, Singapore, Tokyo, Frankfurt, and Hong Kong (no Seoul).
qwen3.8-max is priced at $2 per 1M input tokens and $6 per 1M output tokens for the International scope.
Access to Agent/Workflow/Knowledge base/Application-Calling pages in Singapore is restricted to users who created applications before April 21, 2025.
Model Studio publishes four text-generation interfaces: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, OpenAI-compatible Responses, Anthropic-compatible Messages API, and DashScope.
The Responses API has a context limit where max input is approximately 80% of the model's window to reserve room for built-in tool calls and reasoning.
The Assistant API is deprecated.
DashScope Python SDK requires Python version 3.9 or higher.
A DashScope SDK Expert CLI assistant is built into the dashscope Python SDK version 1.27.3 or later, but this feature is China site only.
The workspace-specific OpenAI-compatible base URL format for Singapore is https://{WorkspaceId}.ap-southeast-1.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1.
API keys are region-bound; calling a region's base URL requires a key created in that specific region.
Workspace-dedicated domains exist only for Beijing, Singapore, and Hong Kong.
The legacy DashScope domain stops receiving new features after September 30, 2026.
kimi-k3 does not support the parallel_tool_calls parameter to control whether calls are parallel.
Qwen series models do not support tool_choice="required".
The Qwen-Omni-Realtime series supports neither the tool_choice nor parallel_tool_calls parameters.
Guidance recommends providing no more than 20 tools to the main model for optimal accuracy.
Structured Output JSON Schema mode supported models include Qwen3.8-Max series and Qwen3.8-Flash series.
It is unconfirmed whether the JSON Schema mode in Structured Output uses strict grammar-constrained decoding or best-effort prompt-level enforcement.
Built-in tools are exposed through the Responses API tools array.
Response output items from built-in tools are typed as web_search_call, web_extractor_call, image_search_call, function_call, and mcp_call.
The web_search tool costs $10.00 per 1,000 calls in the Singapore region.
kimi-k3 supports web search only via the Responses API web_search tool, not via enable_search.
qwen3.8-omni-flash supports only the web_search tool among built-in options.
The web_extractor tool must be used together with web_search.
The web_extractor tool is free for a limited time.
The code_interpreter tool is free for a limited time but increases token consumption.
The t2i_search tool costs $8 per 1,000 calls in Singapore.
The t2i_search tool costs $3.44 per 1,000 calls in Beijing.
The image_search tool doc states $8.00 per 1,000 calls, but the region label was truncated, leaving the region unconfirmed.
The file_search tool requires vector_store_ids and currently supports only one knowledge base ID.
Tablestore Knowledge Storage Service offers serverless RAG with up to 100M documents per KB by default.
A Model Studio savings plan does not cover embedding/rerank fees incurred through Knowledge Base.
For Token Plan/Coding Plan harness tools, web search is billed at CNY 29 per 1,000 calls after free calls, but this pricing info is China site only.
Remote MCP servers can be called directly via the Responses API mcp tool using an SSE endpoint.
International availability of a hosted MCP marketplace or Model-Studio-hosted MCP servers is unconfirmed; evidence suggests it is China site only.
Implicit cache-served input tokens are typically billed at 20% of the standard input token price.
Explicit cache creation costs a 25% surcharge over standard input price, and each subsequent hit saves 90%.
The minimum length for implicit cache hits is 1,024 tokens, except for Zhipu-deployed GLM models which require 512 tokens.
Explicit cache requires a minimum of 1,024 tokens of cached content and allows a maximum of 4 cache markers per request.
There is no published TTL for implicit cache; hits depend on cache generation and other factors.
Explicit cache has a TTL of 5 minutes, automatically renewed on each hit.
Cache discount and batch discount cannot apply simultaneously.
Batch API inference is discounted to 50% of the real-time inference price for both input and output tokens.
Batch API is supported only in China (Beijing) and Singapore regions.
Batch API scale limits are up to 50,000 requests per file and max 500 MB per file.
Each JSON line in a Batch API file must be ≤ 6 MB.
Batch API requests are not subject to real-time rate limiting.
The official turnaround SLA number for Batch API is unconfirmed.
Free quota for Batch API is valid for 90 days.
Thinking content is billed as Output Tokens.
The thinking_budget parameter sets the maximum number of tokens for the reasoning process.
Accepted values for reasoning_effort levels (low, medium, xhigh) are unconfirmed on alibabacloud.com.
Rate limits are applied at the Alibaba Cloud account level, aggregating usage across all RAM users, workspaces, and API keys.
HTTP 429 indicates rate limiting, while HTTP 403 indicates quota exhaustion.
qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash have fixed limits of 30,000 RPM and 5,000,000 TPM under Global scope.
qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash use Dynamic Rate Limiting under International/Singapore scope.
Dynamic rate limiting tiers are based on monthly spend: Tier 1 ≤ $8,000; Tier 2 $8,000–$140,000; Tier 3 > $140,000.
Temporary TPM quota increases in the console take effect immediately and last 30 days, according to third-party reports (unconfirmed officially).
Model Studio runs content-safety moderation inline with inference.
Blocked content returns HTTP 400 with error code DataInspectionFailed (DashScope) or data_inspection_failed (OpenAI-compatible).
There is no documented off switch for platform-level Green Net inspection; it is treated as always on.
AI Guardrails is a separate, customer-configurable layer available in Asia Pacific SE 1 (Singapore).
Alibaba Cloud will never use customer data for model training.
Default retention for user prompts and responses is no longer than 30 days unless required by law.
Zero Data Retention (ZDR) is available to enterprise customers of Alibaba Cloud International Site at the workspace level.
The ZDR approval process involving an account manager and needs assessment is unconfirmed on official pages.
Singapore region uses the International deployment scope, storing request data in that region.
Model Studio has achieved SOC 2 compliance with an unqualified opinion.
Model-Studio-level ISO 27001/27017/27018 scope is unconfirmed; only platform-level certifications are listed.
PrivateLink access for Model Studio is documented for China (Beijing) and China (Hong Kong) only.
A single Model Studio workspace cannot span geographic regions.
Up to 50 API keys are allowed per account per region, and a primary account can have up to 20 workspaces.
RAM users can view only the API keys in the workspaces they have joined.
Advanced administrative permissions for RAM users were withdrawn in a permission system upgrade notice.
Cost bills can be broken down by API Key ID and workspace ID.
The Assistant API migration path is to the Responses API.
No shutdown date is published for Model Studio's Assistant API (unconfirmed).
Application Calling API uses POST https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/api/v1/apps/{APP_ID}/completion for Singapore.
To manage and call applications in a specific workspace via API, APP ID and Workspace ID must be set at the same time.
New requests sent through the same APP_ID after publishing use the new version's configuration.
Fine-tuning is available in Singapore among international regions.
Free quota is 1M tokens per eligible model for 90 days, applicable only in Singapore region with International deployment scope.
Non-Singapore web_search per-strategy prices (turbo/max/agent/agent_max) are unconfirmed for Virginia, Frankfurt, Tokyo, and Hong Kong.
